text:
eli: Quick check-in — started Argon9b int6 bring-up on a small prod slice. Initial throughput looks promising but saw a few quality outliers on longform summarization. Posting notes and action items below.

maria: what's the perf numbers and unit econ? :eyes: 

samir: ran 5k eval prompts (mix short/long). P95 latency ~420ms on our p4d pool with batching. Tokens/sec ~210. Cost estimate ~ $0.028 per 1k tokens (after batching + kvcache) — rough hosted number.

samir: quality snapshot: ROUGE-L down ~1.1 pts vs baseline 13b-int8 on long summaries, short Q/A unchanged. F1/regression concentrated in the "citation" slice (long documents requiring extraction).

eli: do we have failing examples? can we reproduce locally with a smaller context window?

maria: pasted two failing prompts into the thread (shortened):
- Prompt A: user asks for a 2-line summary of a short news blurb — model hallucinates an extra claim.
- Prompt B: 1.5k token doc -> concise summary: misses a key named entity and drops a citation.

samir: repro command I used:
```
python run_eval.py --model argon9b-int6 --file fail_prompts.json --batch 8 --truncate 2048
```
Run locally with cpu fallback for quick checks.

kevin: about rollout/fallback — proposal: canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% with health gates. If longform slice regression >1.5 pts or user-level complaints spike, route affected traffic to argon9b-int8 variant or 13b baseline.

anya: quick econ note: int6 gives ~35% token-cost reduction vs int8 for the same model/serving config. If we route 30% of traffic to int8 as fallback, net unit savings drop to ~15% (approx). Need precise sheet for GTN.

eli: action items:
- samir: run focused citation slice with 10k samples and post confusion examples + per-slice ROUGE/F1 (due tomorrow)
- maria: compute unit-econ spreadsheet comparing mixes (int6-only, int6+30% int8, int6+dynamic fallback) and include latency tail impacts
- kevin: prepare canary flags + rollback playbook and test on staging

ops-bot: canary deployed argon9b-int6 to prod pool argon-pool-3 at 2026-03-20T16:10Z :rocket:

maria: added preliminary econ sheet (internal): https://redwood.internal/sheets/argon9b-econ — opened comments for assumptions.

samir: quick debugging note — quantization noise seems sensitive to tokenizer normalization. Try re-running eval with `--no-normalize` to isolate.

eli: thanks team. quick sync tomorrow 09:30 PT to review 10k-slice results and decide routing. :thumbsup:
